title: Iron Age settlement
description: Round huts of an Iron Age settlement found in 2016 in the Northern Necropolis area.

title: Phrygian cult centre
description: Phrygians build a temple/cult place of the Mother Goddess (Cybele) at the site; earliest layout of the Ploutonion with a stepped altar above the cave (Phase Ia).
disputed: Date 'probably first half of 7th c. BC' is approximate.

title: Foundation of Hierapolis
description: Greek city founded. Sources disagree: Seleucid foundation (Antiochus I or Antiochus III), or Attalid foundation by Eumenes II of Pergamon after 188 BC; UNESCO says the Attalid kings founded the spa at the end of the 2nd c. BC.
disputed: Founder disputed: Seleucids (Antiochus I 281-261 BC / Antiochus III) vs Attalids (Eumenes II, c.190 BC). The museum displays an imago clipeata of Eumenes II captioned as founder.

title: Treaty of Apamea
description: After the defeat of Antiochus III at Magnesia (190 BC) the region passes to Pergamon under Eumenes II.

title: Coinage and textiles
description: City mints bronze coins (name 'Hieropolis'); famed for wool and dyeing using the spring water.

title: Bequest to Rome
description: Attalus III bequeaths Pergamon to Rome; Hierapolis becomes part of the Roman province of Asia (formally organised 129 BC).
disputed: Province formally organised c. 129 BC after Aristonicus' revolt; '133 BC' is the bequest year.

title: Earthquake under Tiberius
description: A major earthquake damages/destroys the city.
disputed: Commonly repeated; the AD 17 earthquake is attested for 12 cities of Asia (Tacitus Ann. 2.47) but Hierapolis is not named there - treat as uncertain.

title: Birth of Epictetus
description: Stoic philosopher Epictetus born a slave at Hierapolis.

title: Earthquake under Nero
description: Severe earthquake ruins the city; rebuilt in Roman style with imperial support; Ploutonion monumentalised (Phase IIb).
disputed: Tacitus (Ann. 14.27) names Laodicea for AD 60; destruction at Hierapolis rests on archaeology and later tradition.

title: Martyrdom of Philip
description: Tradition places the martyrdom of the apostle Philip at Hierapolis in AD 80.
disputed: Tradition only; identity Apostle vs Evangelist debated since antiquity.

title: Frontinus Gate and Street
description: Proconsul Sextus Julius Frontinus builds the triple gate dedicated to Domitian and the colonnaded main street.

title: Latrine on Frontinus Street
description: Public latrine built just inside the Frontinus Gate.

title: Roman theatre completed
description: Theatre completed under Hadrian (inscription naming Tiberius Julius Myndius); often linked to a visit by Hadrian in 129.
disputed: Hadrianic visit/129 date not securely attested.

title: North Agora and Stoa-basilica
description: North Agora (280 x 170 m) built; Stoa-basilica on its E side late Hadrianic-early Antonine.

title: Severan theatre facade
description: Three-storey scaenae frons with relief friezes (Apollo/Artemis cycles, Dionysus, Severus' family) built under Septimius Severus.
disputed: Some museum captions date reliefs 'end of 2nd c.' or 'end of 3rd c.'.

title: Caracalla and neokoros
description: Caracalla visits and grants the neokoros title.
disputed: Repeated by Wikipedia/TAN; primary attestation not checked.

title: Nymphaeum of the Tritons
description: Monumental fountain on Frontinus Street dated by inscription to Severus Alexander.

title: Sawmill relief
description: Sarcophagus of Marcus Aurelius Ammianos shows a water-powered stone sawmill - earliest known crank and connecting rod.

title: Theatre aquatic conversion
description: Major works on the scene building; orchestra made watertight (kolymbethra) for aquatic shows.

title: Last imperial visit
description: Emperor Valens visits during his Persian campaign - the last imperial visit.

title: Christianisation; Ploutonion closed
description: Ploutonion entrance filled/walled; earthquake damage to Agora; Ploutonion functional until 4th c.

title: Theodosian walls and gates
description: City wall circuit with North and South Byzantine gates, partly built from Agora stone.

title: Martyrium of St Philip
description: Octagonal martyrium built on the hill NE of the city; burned late 5th/early 6th c.

title: Metropolitan see
description: Justinian raises the bishop of Hierapolis to metropolitan.

title: Cathedral
description: Three-aisled cathedral with baptistery built.

title: Persian raids and great earthquake
description: Persian armies and a destructive earthquake devastate the city; theatre collapses; Antique Pool takes its present form.
disputed: Exact year not established in sources consulted.

title: Middle Byzantine village
description: Houses and olive-processing installations over the ruins (e.g., Ploutonion Phase V); 11th-c. courtyard house excavated.

title: Seljuk control
description: Area comes under the Seljuk sultanate of Konya.

title: Third Crusade
description: Frederick Barbarossa's crusaders with Byzantine allies take the settlement.

title: Seljuk castle
description: Turks build a fortress on the site (OSM 'Seldjuk Fortress Wall', near museum).

title: Final earthquake
description: Great earthquake ends settlement within the ancient city.
disputed: Britannica gives 1334 for abandonment after an earthquake; Wikipedia's wording is garbled.

title: Laborde publishes views and plan
description: Léon de Laborde's Voyage de l'Asie Mineure publishes a plan of 'Pambouk Kalessi' and engravings of the petrified cascades and ruins.
disputed: Earlier travellers (e.g., 18th c.) also described the site; not catalogued here.

title: Carl Humann's German survey
description: Carl Humann surveys and excavates for about two weeks; city plan dated 24 June-7 July 1887.

title: 'Altertümer von Hierapolis' published
description: Humann, Cichorius, Judeich and Winter publish the results (JdI Ergänzungsheft 4, Berlin, G. Reimer).
disputed: Wikipedia/TAN wrongly give 1889 as publication year.

title: Italian Archaeological Mission (MAIER)
description: Systematic Italian excavations begin under Paolo Verzone; later directors include Francesco D'Andria and Grazia Semeraro.

title: First 'Plutonium' identification
description: Italian archaeologists identify a gas-emitting cave beside the Temple of Apollo as the Plutonium.
disputed: Later superseded by the 2013 identification of the sanctuary with dedicatory inscription.

title: Museum opens in the Great Baths
description: Hierapolis Archaeology Museum installed in the Roman baths.

title: UNESCO World Heritage
description: Hierapolis-Pamukkale inscribed, criteria (iii)(iv)(vii).

title: Theatre restoration
description: Major restoration of the theatre by the Italian mission.

title: Tomb of St Philip announced
description: D'Andria announces a church built around a 1st-c. tomb identified as Philip's, ~40 m from the Martyrium.
disputed: Identification is the excavator's interpretation; tomb empty.

title: Ploutonion rediscovered
description: D'Andria announces the Ploutonion sanctuary (excavated from 2008): dedication to Pluto and Kore, theatron, pool, cave; Cerberus and snake statues found later that year.

title: CO2 study
description: Pfanz et al. publish measurements of lethal CO2 concentrations (up to 91%) at the Ploutonion.
